name: Double encoding (VPF)
corpus: synthetic photo-like scenes generated from fixed seeds (forensic.validation.run.scene)

detection.task: Was the H.264 video decoded and encoded again (VPF footprint of the first GOP)?
detection.positives: 16 10 s clips from four synthetic sources: first encoded with GOP [10, 15, 20, 30] at CRF 26, re-encoded at CRF 22 with GOP 250 (no B-frames) or GOP 100 (2 B-frames)
detection.negatives: 16 clips from the same sources encoded once with the second settings

known_failure_modes: Simulated with x264 on synthetic content; the second encoding at higher quality than the first is the easy case. Recorder firmware and platform transcoders behave differently.
Fails when the second GOP is a multiple of the first or when B-frames dominate; a first GOP of 30 was missed in every 10 s test clip, and two B-frames in the second encoding halve detection.
Re-encoding is not manipulation: it tells you the file is not the recorder's original stream.
